tasks.title: Complete the native single-race lifecycle through results and restart
tasks.question: What is the smallest clean-room state flow that completes one native race from initial start through three laps, finish/results, and a clean restart while reusing the existing race, pause, and rival systems?
acceptance_criteria: Before editing, trace the actual initial, racing, paused, lap-crossing, finished, results and restart transitions in gamecube-demo/source/main.c, gamecube-demo/source/gameplay_state.h, gamecube-demo/source/pause_state.h and their host tests; distinguish existing behavior from the specific missing results/session transition.

Reuse the existing native lap counter, three-lap finish condition, race/lap timers, best-lap and overtake metrics, pause/restart helpers, route-cursor reset, and the rival implementation integrated by PR #327; do not recreate or replace those systems.

Implement only the smallest explicit, testable session/results state needed for initial start -> active race -> three-lap finish/results -> restart. Pause/resume must remain confined to an active race, and no simulation or timer may advance after the finish.

Show a read-only results view using only measured prototype data, including completed laps, total race time, available last/best lap data and overtake count. Do not invent finishing positions, championship standings, persistent saves or unsupported rival results.

Restart must clear all per-run state consistently, including distance, lap/timing data, finish/results flags, pause, boost/heat, rival placement/overtake state and route cursor; a second run must behave like a fresh first run.

Add host regression tests against the production transition helpers for valid and invalid transitions, the exact three-lap finish, pause/timer freeze, post-finish immutability, results stability and full restart reset; tests must cover relevant boundary cases.

The exact PR head must pass host tests, native GameCube and Wii DOL/ELF builds, artifact validation, and the existing bounded Dolphin checks. Label scripted emulator evidence as scripted; do not claim human-operated or physical-hardware acceptance.
Keep all new code/assets clean-room and source-authored. Do not import Step 102 content, commercial assets, ROM-derived data or PC/N64 code; keep this task limited to the single-race lifecycle.

tasks.title: Measure and optimize the native race frame on GameCube/Wii
tasks.question: Which native race-frame CPU, route-sampling, GX submission or memory costs are actually limiting performance, and what smallest measured optimization improves them without changing gameplay?
acceptance_criteria: Do not start until the race lifecycle, rival progression and front-end flow have passing functional regression tests.
Establish a repeatable baseline for frame time, route sampling, GX submission and memory use on available Dolphin diagnostics and/or real hardware; label unavailable measurements explicitly.
Identify one measured bottleneck with reproducible evidence before changing implementation; do not optimize based only on intuition or source appearance.
Optimize only the demonstrated hot path while preserving deterministic simulation, route continuity, visual output and GameCube/Wii memory constraints.
Add regression tests or deterministic benchmark checks proving behavior is unchanged and the targeted metric improves; reject optimizations without measurable benefit.
Run host tests, GameCube build, headless Dolphin smoke and available frame diagnostics; do not describe headless smoke as visual verification.
Record before/after measurements, target environment, uncertainty and any remaining hardware-only validation.
